x: Alan Jackson and Dudley Gordon were finalists in the 400m. and a welcome entry in the 400m. hurdles was Brian Coleman. In the 3000m. walk our Olympic men Stan Vickers and Eric Hall filled 1st. and 3rd. places.
There were two races over 440 yds, Charlie Jones being second (52 4) in the first one and Alan Jackson winning the second in 52 6 Dave Ansell won the 100 yds in 10 8s. and the long jump with 20'7".
The 440 yds. was easily won by Alan Jackson in 52.6, the second man being timed at 55.4. We defeated Cambridge in the 4 x 110 yds relay, 45.4 to 46.8.

Charlie Jones proved to be the mainstay of our team by winning both 100 and 220 yds in 10.3 and 23.2s. respectively, the long jump with 19'7½" and finishing third in both the shot and discus. Alan Jackson won the 440 yds in the good time of 51.6s. and J. Thresher won the Junior 880 yds in 2m.4.5s.

The next event concerning the Bels was the 440 yds which was run as a straight final, and taking part was our 4 x 440 relay team. Alan Jackson and P. Pepe started rather fast into the mud while Brian Morris and Frank Wright went off steadily.

Charlie Jones took second place in both sprints, clocking 10.2 and 22.9; in the second string Alan Jackson was third in 23.9. In the 440 Dave Mitchell was second in 53.4 whilst Alan Jackson won the second string event in 53.5.

Our 4 x 110 yds. team failed to materialize and in the 4 x 440 yds. we were fifth. Frank Wright, Pat Fox, Alan Jackson and Brian Morris constituted our team. The medley relay saw us finish in 6th place.
Our own Alan Jackson (51·9) was also unable to reach the final but ran a sound race. When he has the courage to make his first 220 a little faster his times will undoubtedly improve.

Brian Morris won the senior 'A' 220 in 23.8 whilst Alan Jackson secured second place in the 'B' with 23.6 - a grand start to the meeting. Dave Mitchell won a well judged quarter in the good time of 52.1 and Alan Black obtained further points by finishing 4th in the 880.

Other good performances were made during the heats on Friday evening by Alan Jackson, with a 51.8 quarter and by Dave Mitchell (another fine prospect) who did a personal best of 1:56.6 in his 880 yds heat.

Alan Jackson was 2nd in the 'A' 100 yds. with 10.9 and Pat Fox represented us in the 'B' event. Jock Cameron, making a welcome return to the track, was runner-up in the 220 yards with a time of 24.5 secs, and both 'A' and 'B' events in the 440 yds were scooped for the Bels. by Alan Jackson, 51.8 and…

Alan Jackson was unable to reproduce the 51.8 he did in his heat and finished 6th, in 53.9 secs. Dereck Johnson ran as he liked to win the 880 yards, moving away from the field at 660, at which point our Dave Mitchell was lying second only to fade badly over the last furlong, and record 2:01 for 6th place.
The first leg, an 880, was run by Dave Mitchell and he handed over to Alan Jackson some twenty yards behind Linford (T.V.H.) and Frank Wright, running for the Police.
Out to prove himself our best quarter miler Gerry LeRoy streaked past the line to win with a time of 49.0 secs, with Alan Jackson 3rd, in a personal best 50.6 secs.

Alan Jackson had a fine win from Buchanan (HHH) in the 300 yards after having finished third, with 10.6 secs., in the short sprint. John Thresher and Dereck Crookes gave us max. points in the Senior ¾ mile, and with some doubling up in other events we eventually amassed 60 points, as follows:
CENTRE LEFT: Alan Jackson wins Club 880 yards championship from John Thresher. CENTRE RIGHT: Clive Shippen leads at the water-jump in the "Brockman" steeplechase.

Trevor Tolson ran in the 100 yards, Dave Carter the 220, Alan Jackson and John Thresher the 880, and Clive Shippen the steeplechase. Peter Eldridge was one of two athletes to suffer at the hands of a poor starter in the 440 yards final, and although well down at the start still managed to finish 3rd.
Randy Glenn, Terry Newell and Alan Jackson produced a blanket finish for 2nd, 3rd and 4th, all recording 51.5. The hardest fought race of the day was the Senior 880 yards.

Of the "B" and "C" teams, Eric Penny and Fred Paget showed good form, and Alan Jackson's effort was most useful.
